relations.subject: Chagdud Tulku
relations.evidence: In 1945, shortly after completing his first three-year retreat, he went to see Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö. From him, Chagdud tulku received the rinchen terdzö (Tibetan: རིན་ཆེན་གཏེར་མཛོད་) empowerments

relations.subject: Chagdud Tulku
relations.evidence: By 1946 he entered his second three-year retreat, this time under the guidance of the Tromge Trungpa Rinpoche.

relations.subject: Chagdud Tulku
relations.evidence: attended empowerments given by Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje, who became a main teacher as well as a source of spiritual inspiration for him.

relations.subject: Chagdud Tulku
relations.evidence: After this in 1957 he stayed for a year in Lhasa, Tibet, in the same household as Khenpo Dorje, whom he regarded as his root lama.

relations.subject: Chagdud Tulku
relations.evidence: At this location he met Jangchub Dorje, a primary disciple of Apong Terton and a lineage holder of this great tertön's Red Tara cycle. Jangchub Dorje gave him empowerments for the Red Tara cycle

relations.subject: Chagdud Tulku
relations.evidence: He continued to stay in Nepal on into 1978 in order to attend a new series of empowerments in the Chokling Tersar cycle given by Dilgo Khyentse.

relations.subject: Lama Drimed Norbu
relations.evidence: In 1995, Chagdud Rinpoche ordained western teacher Lama Padma Drimed Norbu (Alwyn Fischel), authorized him to teach Dzogchen, and recognized him as his Dzogchen lineage holder.
